- `self.mic_channels`: Which input of the microphone device is recorded. Both inputs mixed suits most microphones; on a two-input interface with the microphone plugged into one input, choose that input so it is recorded at full level in both ears.
- `self.reader`: The screen reader whose speech Studio keeps private. Its speech is left out of the recording unless you put Screen reader speech in.
- `self.exclude_reader`: When System sound is in the recording, record everything except your screen reader. Studio's own sounds are silenced while it records the system.
- `self.camera_on`: Record your camera too. It is off unless you turn it on, and the camera opens only while you check its framing or record.
- `self.camera`: Which camera to record.
- `self.position`: Which corner of the video shows your camera picture, or Camera only to record the camera instead of the screen picture.
- `self.camera_size`: How wide the camera picture is, as a share of the video.
- `self.face_alerts`: While recording, Studio says when your face leaves the camera's view and when it returns, using face detection that runs on this computer. When your screen reader's speech is being recorded, Studio adds a marker instead of speaking.
- `self.mirrored`: Turn this on if positioning advice sends you the wrong way: some cameras flip their picture left to right.
- `self.camera_check_button`: Open the camera and hear, as you move, whether your face is in view and centred, and which way to move. Nothing is recorded or saved.
- `self.fps`: 30 suits most demonstrations. 60 is smoother and needs a display target and desktop duplication; 15 makes smaller files.
- `self.ceiling`: Native size keeps every pixel. 1080p or 720p scales a larger picture down, keeping its shape, for smaller files.
- `self.countdown`: Seconds Studio counts down aloud before recording begins, so you can move to the program you are demonstrating. 0 starts at once.
- `self.pointer`: Draw the mouse pointer in the video.
- `self.folder`: An absolute folder for the video and its check reports. An existing file is never replaced.
- `browse`: Choose the save folder.
- `self.stems`: Beside the video, keep one WAV per sound source for later editing.
- `self.keep_awake`: Stop the computer sleeping, the screen turning off and the screen saver starting while you record or stream. Released as soon as you stop.
- `self.do_not_disturb`: Silence Windows notifications so none slides into the picture or the sound. Studio puts Do Not Disturb back the way it was when you stop, even after a crash.
- `self.show_status`: Studio keeps its windows out of the recording, which can also hide them from a magnifier and from screen sharing. Check this to keep the Recording status window visible; it is then recorded too if it is inside what you record.
- `self.silent_track`: Some websites refuse a video with no soundtrack. On adds a silent one when no sound source is in the recording; off leaves the soundtrack out.
- `self.sound_format`: The kind of file Studio saves when there is no picture, only sound. M4A suits most uses; WAV and FLAC keep every detail; Opus is smallest for speech.
- `self.check_button`: Check everything before recording: the target, a trial picture, each sound source, the microphone, the camera, FFmpeg, the folder and its free space. The result appears below and is read once.
- `test`: Record a short test with exactly these settings to a temporary file, check it the same way as a real recording, and offer to play it. The test file is deleted afterwards.
- `self.test_seconds`: How long the test records, from 5 seconds to 10 minutes. A longer test is a rehearsal: it shows whether the settings hold up.
- `keys`: Assign system-wide keys to stop, pause, mark and check a recording from inside the program you are demonstrating.
- `self.summary`: What will be recorded, which sounds are in and out, where the file goes, then every problem. Stop means recording cannot start; Warn means it can but may be spoiled. Press Enter here to start recording when nothing stops it.
- `self.start_button`: Start the countdown and record. Available after a check finds no Stop.
- `cancel`: Close without recording.
#### DemoResultDialog (`quill/ui/studio_demo_result.py`)

- `self.text`: Verified means every objective check passed. Needs review means the file plays but something may be spoiled, such as a silent source or black stretches. Failed means a stream is missing or the file does not decode.
- `close`: Close this window.
- `inspect`: Take a picture from the middle of the video and open it in the Screenshot Inspector, to read its text or ask AI about it with your approval.
- `ask`: Ask questions about the whole video or a stretch of it. Nothing is sent until you approve it.
- `captions`: Transcribe the speech on this computer and save captions (SRT and VTT) and a plain transcript beside the file. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- `video`: Turn this sound into a video YouTube accepts, with a picture you choose.
#### RecordingStatusFrame (`quill/ui/studio_demo_status.py`)

- `self.text`: Elapsed time, the sounds being recorded, whether the screen reader is in the recording, dropped frames and disk space left. It updates every second.
- `self.pause_button`: Pause the recording; nothing is recorded until you resume. The same button resumes.
- `marker_button`: Note this moment, with an optional label, in the marker list.
- `self.mute_button`: Silence the microphone in the recording; the device stays open and the muted stretch is marked. Press again to unmute.
- `status_button`: Say the status line now.
- `stop_button`: Stop recording, finish the video, check it and save it.
- `discard_button`: Stop and delete this recording after you confirm.
- `close`: Hide this window; recording continues. Reopen it from the tray or the Capture menu.
#### StudioMixerDialog (`quill/ui/studio_mixer.py`)

- `self.book`: Programs: what each program plays. Devices: your sound cards.
- `close`: Close the mixer. Changes stay as you made them.
- `self.programs`: Each program with sound: whether you hear it and how loud, whether it is playing now, and its sound card. Space mutes or unmutes it; Up and Down choose a program.
- `self.mute`: Mute the selected program for you, or unmute it.
- `self.volume`: The selected program's own volume, 0 to 100 percent. Up and Down change it by 1, Page Up and Page Down by 10.
- `self.card`: Which sound card the selected program plays on, as in Windows Settings. Windows default follows whatever the default device is. Windows remembers the choice.
- `refresh`: Read the programs and sound cards again. F5 does the same.
- `self.playback`: Speakers and headphones Windows can use, and which is the default.
- `self.recording`: Microphones and line inputs, which is the default, and each one's level.
- `self.input_level`: How loud the selected input records, 0 to 100 percent.
- `self.input_mute`: Silence the selected input for every program.
#### PictureVideoDialog (`quill/ui/studio_picture_video.py`)

- `self.shape`: The video's size: YouTube's usual 1920 by 1080, square for social posts, vertical for Shorts, or the picture's own size.
- `self.zoom`: The picture moves gently closer over the video, instead of staying still.
- `self.wave`: A white wave that moves with the sound, so viewers can see sound is playing.
- `self.chapters`: Markers you added while recording become chapters in the video and timestamps in the description. YouTube needs at least three, ten seconds apart.
- `self.title_field`: The video's title, up to 100 characters.
- `self.description`: What viewers read under the video. Chapters are added at the end.
#### VideoQuestionDialog (`quill/ui/studio_video_question.py`)

- `self.video`: The video to ask about.
- `browse`: Choose the video file.
- `self.whole`: Look across the whole video.
- `self.stretch`: Look only between the two times below.
- `self.start`: Where the stretch starts, like 1:05 or 1:02:03.
- `self.end`: Where the stretch ends. Leave empty for the end of the video.
- `self.frames`: More frames show more of what happened; fewer make each frame larger and clearer.
- `self.transcript`: When captions exist beside the video, send what was said in the same stretch with the picture. Make captions from the recording's result window.
#### PictureMakerDialog (`quill/ui/studio_picture_maker.py`)

- `self.words`: First, describe the whole picture. After that, say only what to change, such as make the background darker; every earlier request is kept.
- `self.shape`: Wide for a YouTube video, square for a cover, tall for Shorts.
- `self.make`: Send the description to your AI provider after you approve it, then have the picture described to you.
- `self.list`: Every picture made so far, newest last. Choose one to hear its description.
- `self.description`: What the vision model sees in the picture, from a separate look, not the generator's own claim.
- `self.video`: Use the chosen version as the picture of a YouTube video.
- `self.folder`: Open the folder where the pictures are saved.
- `close`: Close. The pictures stay saved.
#### GoLiveDialog (`quill/ui/studio_go_live.py`)

- `self.kind`: Which kind of server your stream host runs. Your host's settings page says.
- `self.host`: The server's address, such as stream.example.org, without http.
- `self.port`: The server's port, often 8000.
- `self.mount`: Icecast only: the mount point, starting with a slash, such as /live.
- `self.stream_id`: SHOUTcast only: the stream number on the server, usually 1.
- `self.user`: Icecast only: usually source.
- `self.password`: The source password. Studio keeps it in Windows Credential Manager, never in its settings or logs.
- `self.secure`: Only if your server offers TLS. Most radio servers do not.
- `self.title_field`: What listeners and directories see as the stream's name.
- `self.description`: A sentence about the show.
- `self.genre`: Such as Talk, Music or Podcast.
- `self.website`: Your show's web address, if any.
- `self.public`: Off keeps the stream unlisted: only people with the address find it.
- `self.quality`: Speech is smallest; Music sounds best; Custom shows every technical choice below.
- `self.format`: The kind of sound listeners receive. SHOUTcast takes MP3 or AAC.
- `self.bitrate`: Higher sounds better and needs a faster upload.
- `self.channels`: Mono halves the size and suits a single voice.
- `self.rate`: 44100 suits most streams.
- `self.loudness`: An automatic level so the stream sounds even, with a limiter against distortion. Off sends the mix exactly as it is.
- `self.list`: Each sound and whether listeners hear it. Space puts the selected one in or leaves it out. Your screen reader starts left out and asks first.
- `self.level`: How loud the selected sound is in the stream; recordings are separate.
- `self.archive`: Keep a copy as FLAC while you broadcast, even through reconnects.
- `self.folder`: Where the saved copy goes.
- `check`: Check everything before going live. The result is read once.
- `test`: A private two-second test of the address and password. Nobody hears it.
- `self.result`: Where the stream goes, what is in it, then every Stop and Warn.
- `self.go`: Start broadcasting. Available after a check finds no Stop.
- `cancel`: Close without broadcasting.
#### LiveStatusFrame (`quill/ui/studio_live_status.py`)

- `self.text`: On air or reconnecting, time live, sounds in the stream, reconnects.
- `self.now`: The title listeners see. Press Enter or Update the title to send it.
- `send`: Send the now-playing title to the server.
- `self.mute`: Listeners hear silence at once; the connection and any saved copy continue. Press again to unmute.
- `stop_button`: End the broadcast and finish the saved copy.
- `close`: Hide this window; the broadcast continues.

## Quill Inkwell

Control coverage: 5 audited sites (5 helped).

### Every window, and what it is for

**AI Usage.** How much each AI you have set up has been used, one sentence each, and whose count it is. Manage Usage opens the selected one's own page.

**Ask.** A conversation about your abbreviations, on whichever AI is in use: each abbreviation by name and expansion, most used first, goes with every message, and nothing you type in other programs ever does. Type in Your message and press Enter; the reply is read aloud and added to the conversation above. Quick questions holds What do I type most? and a few more.

**Choose Your AI.** Choose where Quill Inkwell's AI comes from: QUILL's free AI, your ChatGPT plan, GitHub Copilot, Codex or your own key. Quill Inkwell signs in on its own, as QUILL Inkwell. The list says which is in use; Enter uses the selected one or signs in to it, and Delete signs a signed-in one out.

**Choose a Document.** Pick the document Suggest Abbreviations reads: plain text, Markdown, Word or rich text. Nothing is sent yet; you are asked first, and Cancel sends nothing.

**Edit Abbreviation.** Change one abbreviation: its trigger word, its expansion, or how it behaves -- which keys fire it, what is spoken, whether a sound plays. The expansion may carry ${cursor}, ${date}, ${time}, and ${clipboard}. OK saves the change into the shared library at once.

**Excluded Applications.** Programs where expansion must never run, one program file name per line -- notepad.exe, for example. Password managers and Windows sign-in prompts are always excluded whether or not you list them. OK saves the list immediately.

**Expand Word Key.** Choose one key that expands the word you just typed, in any program, without waiting for a space or punctuation. There is none until you choose one. Type it, or leave the box empty for no key; a key another QuillVille app already uses is refused, and you are told whose it is.

**Find a Setting or Command.** Every menu command in this app, searchable by name. Type part of a name; Down moves into the matches; Enter does the highlighted one, exactly as choosing it from its menu would. An option says whether it is on, and doing it switches it and says the new state.

**Manage Abbreviations.** Your whole abbreviation library in one place: create, edit, delete, and switch entries on or off, with search and a category filter to find the one you mean. Import and Export move the library as a file. Every change saves immediately and reaches QUILL's editor too, because both apps read the same library.

**New Abbreviation.** Create one abbreviation: the trigger word you will type, and the expansion that replaces it. The expansion may carry placeholders -- ${cursor} for where the caret lands, ${date}, ${time}, and ${clipboard} -- and Expand after chooses which keys fire it, including never, for Quick Insert only. OK saves it into the shared library at once.

**Quick Insert.** Pick an abbreviation and Inkwell types its expansion into the window you were just working in -- the way to use an entry set to expand only manually, or one whose trigger you cannot recall. Filter, choose, press Enter; focus returns to where you were and the text is typed there. If there is nowhere to type, the expansion is copied to the clipboard instead.

**Quick Insert Key.** Choose one key that opens Quick Insert from any program, so an entry you only insert by hand is always a keystroke away. There is none until you choose one. Type it, or leave the box empty for no key; a key another QuillVille app already uses is refused, and you are told whose it is.

**Quill Inkwell.** The manager window for a service that lives in the system tray: type an abbreviation in any application -- a browser, a mail client, a form -- and Inkwell replaces it with the text you saved. The list shows your library, which is the same library QUILL's editor expands from, so an abbreviation added in either works in both immediately. Closing this window keeps expansion running in the tray unless you turn that off in Options.

**Send the Document?.** Whether the text of the document you picked goes to the AI in use, and how much of it. The file's name and folder stay on this computer. No is the default and sends nothing.

**Show and Hide Key.** Choose one key that shows and hides the Inkwell window from any program. Type it, for example with Ctrl, Alt and Shift held, or leave the box empty for no key. A key another QuillVille app already uses is refused, and you are told whose it is.

**Sign In to Your AI.** Sign in to the AI you chose. Open the Page takes you to its sign-in page; approve there, and this closes itself once you are signed in.

**Suggest Abbreviations.** The abbreviations the AI suggested from your document, one check box each, all starting cleared. Check the ones you want and press OK to add them to the library QUILL shares; Cancel adds none. An abbreviation you already have is never suggested, so nothing here can replace one of yours.

**Update downloaded.** A new Quill Inkwell is on disk and ready. Install and restart now applies it and relaunches -- your abbreviations and settings are kept -- or Open folder shows you the installer to run later.

**Windows titled "Help:...".** This is the help window itself: the purpose of the window you were in, then the control you were on. Escape returns you to it.

### Every authored control help sentence

#### QuillInkwellFrame (`quill/apps/inkwell.py`)

- `self._list`: Your abbreviation library, read-only here: each row is a trigger word, the start of what it expands to, and its category, with disabled entries marked. To add, change, or remove entries press the Manage Abbreviations button (Ctrl+M); this list follows the same library QUILL's editor expands from.
- `manage_btn`: Open the Manage Abbreviations dialog: create, edit, delete, enable or disable entries, and import or export the whole library. Changes save immediately and work in QUILL too.
- `quick_btn`: Pick an abbreviation and have its expansion typed into the window you were just working in -- the way to use entries set to expand only manually. Also on Ctrl+K here, and from any program on the key you choose with File, Quick Insert Key.
#### SuggestionsDialog (`quill/apps/inkwell_suggest_dialog.py`)

- `ok`: Add the abbreviations you checked to your library, the same library QUILL expands from, and close. If none are checked, nothing is added.
- `cancel`: Close without adding any of the suggested abbreviations.
- `box`: Check this to add the abbreviation to your library when you press OK. It starts cleared, so nothing the AI suggested is added unless you check it. You can change or delete it later in Manage Abbreviations.

## QUILL Transcribe

Control coverage: 44 audited sites (44 helped).

### Every window, and what it is for

**AI Usage.** How much each AI you have set up has been used, one sentence each, and whose count it is. Manage Usage opens the selected one's own page.

**Ask.** A conversation about your dictation, on whichever AI is in use: the transcript you last reviewed, or this session's dictated phrases, go with every message, never your voice. Type in Your message and press Enter; the reply is read aloud and added to the conversation above. Quick questions holds Who said what? and a few more.

**Choose Microphone.** The microphone QUILL Transcribe listens on. The Windows default follows whatever Windows is set to; a named microphone stays chosen.

**Choose Model.** Every speech model QUILL knows, each marked as running on this computer or sending your speech over the internet, with its languages and whether it is downloaded. The model you choose is used every time until you choose another.

**Choose Your AI.** Choose where QUILL Transcribe's AI comes from: QUILL's free AI, your ChatGPT plan, GitHub Copilot, Codex or your own key. QUILL Transcribe signs in on its own, as QUILL Transcribe. The list says which is in use; Enter uses the selected one or signs in to it, and Delete signs a signed-in one out.

**Dictation Commands.** Everything dictation understands, to read with the arrow keys. In another program only the commands that do not need to read its text work.

**Dictation Profile.** Choose the kind of writing dictation is for: Standard, Email, Document, Markdown, Chat, Coding or Verbatim. A profile sets the pause, fillers and punctuation, and how headings, bold and italic are written.

**Dictation Settings.** The dictation settings QUILL Transcribe uses: the model, microphone, language, punctuation, and what you hear after each phrase. They are the same settings as dictation in QUILL and QUILL Lite, kept for this app.

**Discard These Words.** The AI has changed these words. Yes throws them away and writes nothing; No keeps the review open.

**Exit QUILL Transcribe.** Dictation is paused with words that were never written. Exit throws them away and closes QUILL Transcribe; Cancel keeps it running so you can resume.

**Find a Setting or Command.** Every menu command in this app, searchable by name. Type part of a name; Down moves into the matches; Enter does the highlighted one.

**Go back to Stable?.** How to come back to Stable from a newer version. When Stable can read everything you have saved, you can go back now. When it can't, you can wait for Stable to catch up, or go back to the copy saved when you joined. Close changes nothing.

**Going straight back isn't safe yet.** How to come back to Stable from a newer version. When Stable can read everything you have saved, you can go back now. When it can't, you can wait for Stable to catch up, or go back to the copy saved when you joined. Close changes nothing.

**Import Words.** What the file would add to your list, with the counts. Add Them adds them; nothing you already have is replaced.

**More Dictation Settings.** The rest of dictation's settings: pauses, fillers, dashes, wake phrase and the OpenAI model. Some only matter inside QUILL's own documents.

**Move QUILL Transcribe to Beta?.** Says plainly what could go wrong on Beta or Dev, how your settings are protected, and how to come back. Nothing changes unless you check the box and choose Move.

**Move QUILL Transcribe to Dev?.** Says plainly what could go wrong on Beta or Dev, how your settings are protected, and how to come back. Nothing changes unless you check the box and choose Move.

**My Words and Phrases.** The words, phrases and corrections dictation uses, the same list as QUILL. Import adds the new entries from a Markdown or CSV file after showing them; Export saves the list to one.

**Notifications.** Finished, failed and cancelled transcriptions. Open one to review its transcript.

**Practice Dictation.** A field of QUILL Transcribe's own that dictation types into, so you can learn and test dictation without writing into another program. Start Dictation Here starts it in the field; Read This Sentence reads a sentence aloud and says how many words were heard as you said them.

**QUILL Transcribe.** QUILL Transcribe types what you say into the program you are using. This window shows whether dictation is on, which model and microphone it uses, and what happened last. Start dictation from your start and stop key or the tray menu; it writes only into the field you started in, and pauses if you move. Closing this window keeps QUILL Transcribe in the tray.

**QUILL Transcribe Tutorials.** Five short lessons: a first dictation in the Practice window, pausing and resuming, commands with the command word, snippets by voice, and review. Try It runs a step's command for you.

**Release Channel: QUILL Transcribe.** Choose which versions this app offers you: Stable, the one we recommend; Beta, new features a few weeks early; or Dev, work in progress for testers. Arrowing through the choices only explains them -- nothing changes until you choose Switch.

**Review Dictation.** Dictated words wait here before they are inserted. Read them, type or keep dictating to change them, ask the AI to change them if AI is on, and hear what changed. Control Enter inserts them where they were going; nothing is written before that.

**Review Transcript.** A finished transcript of a recording, read-only. Type it, or the part you selected, into a field in another program; copy it, save it as a text file, or open it in QUILL. Nothing is copied or typed anywhere unless you choose it.

**Review with AI.** Before the first change is asked for, this says who receives the words being reviewed and what is sent. No is the default and sends nothing.

**Save Transcript As.** Choose where to save the transcript as a plain text file.

**Send this recording to OpenAI?.** Before a recording goes to OpenAI, this says what is sent. No sends nothing.

**Set Up QUILL Transcribe.** Choose your microphone, the speech model and, if you want one, the key that starts and stops dictation from any program. Finish keeps your choices; Skip changes nothing. Nothing listens and nothing downloads here.

**Show and Hide Key.** Choose one key that shows and hides the QUILL Transcribe window from any program, or leave the box empty for no key. A key another QuillVille app already uses is refused, and you are told whose it is.

**Sign In to Your AI.** Sign in to the AI you chose. Open the Page takes you to its sign-in page; approve there, and this closes itself once you are signed in.

**Speech Models.** The Model Library: download, check or remove the optional speech models. Each download shows its size first, is checked before it is used, and can be cancelled. A model that did not finish is never marked ready.

**Speech Providers.** Use a speech service you already have an account with -- Azure, Google, Amazon, Deepgram and others -- for dictation. Choose one to see what it can do and what it needs, enter that, test it, and save it; keys go to Windows Credential Manager. Then choose it as the speech engine in Dictation Settings.

**Start and Stop Key.** Choose the key that starts and stops dictation from any program. It is Alt+Shift+Backslash unless you change it. Type another, press Record Key to press it instead, or leave the box empty for no key; a key another QuillVille app already uses is refused, and you are told whose it is.

**Transcribe a Recording.** Choose a recording and a model; it is transcribed in the background and the transcript waits in Notifications for you to review.

**Update History: QUILL Transcribe.** A plain record of what the updater did for this app: checks, downloads, channel changes and the copies of your settings it saved. Read-only; nothing here changes anything.

**Update downloaded.** A new QUILL Transcribe is on disk and ready. Install and restart applies it and relaunches -- your settings are kept -- or Open folder shows the installer.

**Use OpenAI.** Before your speech goes to OpenAI, this says what is sent and where. No keeps the model you had; nothing is sent unless you agree.

**Windows titled "Help:...".** This is the help window itself: the purpose of the window you were in, then the control you were on. Escape returns you to it.

### Every authored control help sentence

#### QuillTranscribeFrame (`quill/apps/transcribe.py`)

- `self._state_text`: What dictation is doing now: Ready, Listening, Hearing you, Paused with words held, Waiting for you to switch to a field, or Listening for your wake phrase. The tray icon's name says the same, and Alt+F9 says it with the program, the model and what is held.
- `self._start_button`: Starts dictation in the next field you switch to, or stops it. From another program, your start and stop key does the same without coming here.
- `self._resume_button`: When dictation is paused: writes the held words into the field you started in, once you are back there, and carries on.
- `self._here_button`: When dictation is paused: makes the field you switch to next the one dictation writes into, after the same safety checks as a new start.
- `self._discard_button`: When dictation is paused: throws away the words held while paused. Dictation stays paused until you resume or stop.
- `self._setup_text`: The speech model, microphone, dictation profile and start and stop key dictation uses now. The model you chose is the one that runs; it never changes on its own.
- `self._next_text`: What starting dictation will do, why it paused or could not start, and the last thing it said.
- `self._ai_text`: Which AI is in use, as Which AI Am I Using says it. Press Enter to open Choose Your AI.
- `model_button`: Choose the speech model: each is marked as running on this computer or sending your speech over the internet.
- `mic_button`: Choose the microphone dictation listens on.
- `settings_button`: Language, punctuation, fillers, pauses and what you hear after each phrase: the same settings as dictation in QUILL.
#### ProfileDialog (`quill/apps/transcribe_coach.py`)

- `self.list`: The kind of writing dictation is for. Standard is your Dictation Settings as they are. A profile changes the pause, the filler words and the punctuation, and how headings, bold and italic are written.
- `self.about`: What the profile you are on changes, in one sentence.
- `self.lock`: When this is on, saying QUILL chat mode or another profile's name does not switch profiles. You can still choose one here.
- `ok`: Use the chosen profile from the next phrase on.
- `cancel`: Keep the profile you have.
#### SetupDialog (`quill/apps/transcribe_dialogs.py`)

- `self.intro`: What QUILL Transcribe does and does not do, to read with the arrow keys. Tab moves on to the choices.
- `self.microphone`: The microphone QUILL Transcribe listens on. The Windows default follows whatever Windows is set to; a named one stays chosen.
- `self.test_button`: Records four seconds on the chosen microphone and says how loud it was and what it heard. The recording stays on this computer and is not kept.
- `self.test_result`: What the last microphone test found.
- `self.model`: The model that turns your speech into text. Only models already on this computer are listed here; more can be downloaded later from the Model Library. The one you choose is used every time until you change it.
- `self.advice`: The model that suits this computer and why, as an estimate. It is only advice: the model you choose above is the one used.
- `self.key`: The key that starts and stops dictation from any program: Alt+Shift+\ unless you change it. Type another, for example Ctrl+Alt+PageDown, press Record Key to press it instead, or leave the box empty to use the tray menu only.
- `self.record_key`: Press a key combination and it is written into the start and stop key box. A key another program already uses may not arrive: type that one.
- `self.command_key`: Optional. Press this key in the field you are dictating into and the next thing you say is a command, as if you had said QUILL first: press it, then say scratch that. Press it twice for command mode. Empty unless you choose one; saying QUILL before a command works without it.
- `self.record_command`: Press a key combination and it is written into the command key box.
- `self.at_login`: Opens QUILL Transcribe in the tray when you sign in, so your key works straight away. It does not start listening until you start dictation.
- `finish`: Keep these choices and close setup.
- `skip`: Close setup without changing anything. Setup is on the Help menu whenever you want it.
#### ChooseModelDialog (`quill/apps/transcribe_dialogs.py`)

- `self.list`: Every speech model QUILL knows. Each says whether it runs on this computer or sends your speech over the internet, its tier (Lightweight, Balanced or High accuracy), which languages it knows, and whether it is downloaded. Enter uses the one you are on.
- `self.details`: The model you are on: where it runs, its tier, its languages and size, who publishes it and under which licence.
- `self.advice`: The model that suits this computer and why: whether it keeps up, about how soon your words appear after you pause, its tier and its size. The figures are estimates, and it is only advice: nothing changes until you choose.
- `use`: Make this your model. It is used every time you dictate until you choose another; QUILL Transcribe never switches on its own.
- `library`: Download, check or remove the optional models. Downloads are your choice, show their size first, and are checked before they are used.
- `cancel`: Keep the model you have.
#### TranscriptReviewDialog (`quill/apps/transcribe_files.py`)

- `self.text`: The transcript, read-only. Read it with the arrow keys; select part of it and press Ctrl+C to copy just that part.
- `type_in`: Type the transcript, or only the part you selected, into another program. Switch to the field you want and it is typed there, with the same checks as dictation: never into a password field or a program on your never-type list.
- `copy`: Put the whole transcript on the clipboard.
- `save`: Save the transcript as a text file where you choose.
- `quill`: Open the transcript in QUILL to edit it.
- `close`: Close the transcript. It stays in Notifications.
#### PracticeDictationFrame (`quill/apps/transcribe_practice.py`)

- `self.sentence`: The sentence for the recognition test. Press Read This Sentence, then read it aloud at your usual pace. Next Sentence gives you another.
- `self.field`: QUILL Transcribe's own field. While dictation is on here, what you say is written into this field and nowhere else. You can type and edit in it too; Control F11 starts and stops dictation here.
- `self.result`: The last recognition test: how many words were right, and any that were heard differently. It is said once when the test finishes.
- `close`: Closes the window. Dictation in the practice field stops; nothing is kept.

## Quill Weather

Control coverage: 40 audited sites (40 helped).

### Every window, and what it is for

**AI Usage.** How much each AI you have set up has been used, one sentence each, and whose count it is. Manage Usage opens the selected one's own page.

**Add Weather Location.** Save a new place to watch. Type a ZIP code, city, county, or address and press Search; the matching places come back as a list so same-named towns are told apart, and Add Selected saves the one you choose. A bare latitude,longitude pair resolves to that exact point with no search.

**Ask.** A conversation about the weather, on whichever AI is in use: your primary place's name, never its coordinates, the current conditions, the next hours, the forecast and any active alerts by their official names go with every message. Type in Your message and press Enter; the reply is read aloud and added to the conversation above. Quick questions holds Do I need a coat at 5? and a few more.

**Choose Your AI.** Choose where Quill Weather's AI comes from: QUILL's free AI, your ChatGPT plan, GitHub Copilot, Codex or your own key. Quill Weather signs in on its own, as QUILL Weather. The list says which is in use; Enter uses the selected one or signs in to it, and Delete signs a signed-in one out.

**Customize Quill Weather Features.** Turn whole areas of Quill Weather on or off -- alert monitoring, NOAA Weather Radio. Turning one off removes its menu items at the next launch; nothing you have saved is deleted.

**Quill Weather.** The main window of the weather watcher. Its real work happens in the background: it monitors official National Weather Service alerts for your saved locations and speaks new warnings as they are issued, even from the system tray. The three buttons open the full Weather Center, start or stop the watch, and add a place to watch; closing the window keeps monitoring in the tray by default.

**Quill Weather Tutorials.** Guided lessons, one step at a time, that can run the step for you and notice when you have done it. The contents list is grouped by track and remembers where you stopped; typing 'here' in the filter box narrows it to the tutorials about the window you came from. Follow me watches what the app is doing -- never which key you pressed -- and moves you on by itself.

**Should I Go Out?.** The AI's answer to Should I Go Out?, in plain words, from the forecast for your primary place. Any active alert comes first, in the Weather Service's own words, never reworded by the AI. Copy puts the answer on the clipboard.

**Show and Hide Key.** Choose one key that shows and hides Quill Weather from any program. Type it, for example with Ctrl, Alt and Shift held, or leave the box empty for no key. A key another QuillVille app already uses is refused, and you are told whose it is.

**Sign In to Your AI.** Sign in to the AI you chose. Open the Page takes you to its sign-in page; approve there, and this closes itself once you are signed in.

**Weather Center.** The full text weather report for one location at a time, in reading order: active alerts first, then current conditions, the period forecast, the hourly forecast, and the extended daily outlook. Each list pairs with a read-only detail box below it that follows your selection, so arrowing a list reads the full official text. The Location chooser switches places, Refresh re-pulls, and Add Location and Settings open their own windows.

**Weather Settings.** Every weather preference in one place: temperature and wind units, how much forecast to show, which alert severities matter, how often to refresh, what the Quick Weather line includes, and the alert sound. Save applies everything at once; Cancel changes nothing.

**Windows titled "Help:...".** This is the help window itself: the purpose of the window you were in, then the control you were on. Escape returns you to it.

### Every authored control help sentence

#### AddLocationDialog (`quill/ui/weather/add_location_dialog.py`)

- `self._query`: The place to look up. Any of these forms works: a ZIP code (56301), a city (Saint Cloud MN), a county, or a street address. A bare latitude,longitude pair (45.56,-94.16) is used exactly as typed, with no search. Enter searches; clearing the field clears the results.
- `self._search_btn`: Look the typed place up in the free OpenStreetMap US search and fill the results list with the matching places. The search runs in the background; the status line below reports progress.
- `self._results_list`: The places that matched your search, each with enough of its state and county to tell same-named towns apart. Arrow to the one you mean; Enter or Add Selected saves it.
- `self._name`: What Quill Weather should call this place -- Home, Work, Mom's -- in lists, reports, and spoken alerts. Optional: left empty, the place's own name from the search result is used.
- `self._add_btn`: Save the highlighted place to your locations and close this window. Enabled once the results list has something chosen; the first location you save becomes the primary one.
- `cancel_btn`: Close without saving anything. Escape does the same.
#### WeatherSettingsDialog (`quill/ui/weather/settings_dialog.py`)

- `self._temp`: The scale every temperature is shown and spoken in: Fahrenheit (the default) or Celsius. It applies everywhere -- current conditions, forecasts, and the Quick Weather line.
- `self._wind`: The unit wind speeds are shown and spoken in, wherever wind appears: current conditions, forecasts, and the Quick Weather line. Miles per hour is the default.
- `self._periods`: How many forecast periods the Weather Center's Forecast list holds, 1 to 14. The National Weather Service issues two periods per day (Today, Tonight, and so on), so 14 covers the full week.
- `self._daily_days`: How many days the Weather Center's extended Daily outlook covers, up to 16 -- one summary line per day, reaching past the week the period forecast covers. 0 removes the outlook section entirely.
- `self._hourly_hours`: How many hours the Weather Center's Hourly forecast covers, up to 48 -- one line per hour with temperature, sky, and wind. 0 removes the hourly section entirely.
- `self._severity`: The least severe alert worth showing you. Show all alerts (the default) includes everything the National Weather Service issues; each step up hides the tiers below it, so Extreme only keeps just the worst. Hidden alerts are filtered from the Weather Center and from spoken announcements alike.
- `self._refresh`: How many minutes pass between automatic re-fetches of the weather data, 1 to 180. A shorter interval is fresher; the default of 15 is plenty for observations that update about hourly.
- `self._alert_sound_path`: The sound file that plays when a new alert is announced -- read-only; use Choose to pick a different .wav file. It reads (default chime) when no file of your own is set.
- `choose_btn`: Pick your own alert sound: a .wav file from anywhere on this computer. It is not copied -- moving or deleting the file later falls back to the default chime.
- `play_btn`: Hear the alert sound as it is currently set -- your chosen file or the default chime, repeated the number of times set below -- before you save.
- `default_btn`: Forget the chosen sound file and go back to the built-in default chime.
- `self._alert_sound_repeat`: How many times the alert sound plays in a row when a new alert arrives, 1 to 10. The default is once; more repeats make an alert harder to miss from another room.
- `self._muted`: Alert events you never want to see or hear, one exact event name per line -- for example Rip Current Statement. The name must match what the National Weather Service issues, as shown in the Weather Center's alerts list. Empty (the default) hides nothing.
- `ok`: Save every setting in this window and close it. Changes apply immediately -- an open Weather Center re-renders with the new preferences.
- `cancel_btn`: Close without changing any setting. Escape does the same.
#### WeatherCenterDialog (`quill/ui/weather/weather_center_dialog.py`)

- `self._location_choice`: Which saved place this whole window reports on. Choosing one makes it the primary location -- the one the alert watch and Quick Weather follow -- and fetches its weather right away. Delete removes the chosen place.
- `self._refresh_btn`: Fetch this location's weather again right now -- alerts, conditions, and every forecast. The status line at the bottom says where the data came from and how fresh it is.
- `self._add_btn`: Open Add Weather Location: search by ZIP code, city, county, or address and save a new place. It joins the Location chooser as soon as it is added.
- `self._remove_btn`: Delete the place chosen in the Location list, immediately and without a confirmation. Pressing Delete in the Location list does the same.
- `self._settings_btn`: Open Weather Settings: units, how much forecast to show, alert filtering, refresh cadence, and the alert sound. Saved changes re-render this window immediately.
- `self._alerts_list`: Every alert in effect for this location right now, one line each: the event, the area, and its tier. Arrowing to a row fills the read-only box below with the full official text -- headline, instructions, and timing.
- `self._alert_detail`: The full official text of the alert highlighted in the list above: headline, severity, area, timing, instructions, and description, exactly as issued. Read-only and copyable; it follows the list selection.
- `self._current`: The weather right now at this location, as one readable block: temperature and sky always, plus whichever details you have turned on in Settings -- feels-like, wind, humidity, sunrise, and more. Read-only and copyable, with the observation time at the end.
- `self._forecast_list`: The official forecast, one line per period -- Today, Tonight, and so on -- with its temperature and a short summary. Arrowing to a period fills the read-only box below with its full detailed forecast. Settings chooses how many periods appear.
- `self._period_detail`: The full detailed forecast for the period highlighted in the list above, with abbreviations spelled out for speech. Read-only and copyable; it follows the list selection.
- `self._hourly_list`: Hour-by-hour forecast, one line per hour with time, temperature, sky, and wind. Settings chooses how many hours it covers, up to 48, or turns the section off.
- `self._hourly_detail`: The highlighted hour's line as read-only, copyable text that wraps instead of scrolling off the edge. It follows the hourly list's selection.
- `self._daily_list`: A longer-range outlook, one summary line per day, reaching past the week the period forecast covers. Settings chooses how many days it holds, up to 16, or turns the section off.
- `self._daily_detail`: The highlighted day's line as read-only, copyable text that wraps instead of scrolling off the edge. It follows the daily outlook's selection.
- `self._status`: Where this report came from and how it is doing: the National Weather Service office and zone, the observing station, and any note about data that could not be fetched. Read-only; it updates with every refresh.
- `close_btn`: Close the Weather Center. Escape does the same, and alert monitoring keeps running without it.
#### WeatherAppFrame (`quill/apps/weather.py`)

- `self._open_center_btn`: Open the Weather Center: the full text report for a saved location -- active alerts, current conditions, and the forecasts. Monitoring keeps running whether or not it is open.
- `self._toggle_monitor_btn`: Turn the background alert watch on or off. On, Quill Weather polls the National Weather Service for your saved locations and speaks each new alert as it is issued; the label always shows which way the button will turn it.
- `self._add_location_btn`: Add a place to watch, by ZIP code, city, county, or address. The first location you add becomes the primary one the alert watch follows.

## Quill Converter

Control coverage: 38 audited sites (38 helped).

### Every window, and what it is for

**AI Usage.** How much each AI you have set up has been used, one sentence each, and whose count it is. Manage Usage opens the selected one's own page.

**Ask.** A conversation about your queued files, on whichever AI is in use: each file's details as File Properties gives them, by name and never its folder, the Convert to choice and the last conversion's report go with every message. The AI never hears the sound itself. Type in Your message and press Enter; the reply is read aloud and added to the conversation above. Quick questions holds Will this play in my car?, Make this smaller without losing much, and a few more.

**Auphonic Work Waiting.** Productions Auphonic accepted whose results have not been saved yet, remembered on this computer without contacting Auphonic. Resume waits for them and saves the results; Dismiss forgets one here, and it stays in your Auphonic account.

**Chapter Workbench.** Edit the chapters of an MP3, M4B or M4A: hear it, then add, rename, move, split and merge chapters at the playhead, find them at the pauses, or import and export a chapter list. Save writes them into the file itself, and every later conversion carries them.

**Choose Your AI.** Choose where Quill Converter's AI comes from: QUILL's free AI, your ChatGPT plan, GitHub Copilot, Codex or your own key. Quill Converter signs in on its own, as QUILL Converter. The list says which is in use; Enter uses the selected one or signs in to it, and Delete signs a signed-in one out.

**Conversion Report.** Your last conversion, file by file: the settings used, where the files went, what converted, and why anything failed -- in plain words, then FFmpeg's own message. Copy All puts it on the clipboard, ready to paste into an email to support.

**Convert Audio.** The full conversion dialog, seeded with your queue: every format the main window offers, video included, plus exact settings -- bit rate, sample rate, channels, loudness -- and what to do when an output file already exists. It converts with its own settings, so the main window's effects do not apply here; anything you leave alone keeps the preset's answer.

**Convert from URL.** Paste a web link -- YouTube and many other sites -- and its audio is downloaded and handed to the converter. The page's best audio stream is fetched and nothing else about the page is kept; only download what you have the right to use. A playlist or a channel link asks how much of it to take. Unavailable in Safe Mode.

**Custom Effects.** Every effect on one page, starting from the effect recipe you had chosen: cleanup, tone, leveling, a loudness target, gain, speed, fades, and keeping only part of each file. OK makes these your Custom effects for the next conversion and for Preview; Cancel changes nothing.

**Download a Playlist or Channel.** The link is a playlist or a YouTube channel. Choose how much of it to download -- the whole playlist or the first few, a channel's newest videos, Shorts or live streams, from any date or only recent ones. Every video's audio joins the queue in order, tagged as one album, and pasting the same link later fetches only what is new.

**File Properties.** What is inside the file you highlighted, in plain words: its length and size, its tags, each video, audio and subtitle track, whether it has cover art, and its chapters. It is read-only, and Copy All puts it on the clipboard.

**Find a Setting or Command.** Every menu command in this app, searchable by name. Type part of a name; Down moves into the matches; Enter does the highlighted one, exactly as choosing it from its menu would. An option says whether it is on, and doing it switches it and says the new state.

**Keyboard Shortcuts.** Every key in Quill Converter, grouped by menu, in one read-only list you can arrow through or copy. It is a reference; nothing here changes a key.

**Process with Auphonic.** Send the queue's sound files to your own Auphonic account to be post-produced online, then save the results here. Choose separate productions or one multitrack production, check your account to load your presets, and pick the processing and the output format. Nothing is uploaded until you confirm on the next page.

**Quill Converter.** Convert audio and video between formats: sound to sound, video to sound, or video to video. Queue your files or folders, choose a format, a preset and any effects -- Preview lets you hear fifteen seconds of the result first -- and Convert. Everything runs on this computer, your originals are never touched, and a file already in the output folder is numbered around, never overwritten. The one exception is Process with Auphonic, which uploads only after you confirm.

**Send to Auphonic?.** The last look before anything leaves this computer: every file to be uploaded and every file left out, the preset and processing, and where the results will be saved. Upload and Process sends them using your Auphonic credits; Cancel sends nothing.

**Show and Hide Key.** Choose one key that shows and hides Quill Converter from any program. Type it, for example with Ctrl, Alt and Shift held, or leave the box empty for no key. A key another QuillVille app already uses is refused, and you are told whose it is.

**Sign In to Your AI.** Sign in to the AI you chose. Open the Page takes you to its sign-in page; approve there, and this closes itself once you are signed in.

**Tag Editor.** Every tag of one MP3, M4A, M4B or MP4 file, over five pages -- title, artist and album, the people, the dates and numbers, sorting, and the cover art. Control+Tab moves between pages. OK writes the tags into the file; the sound itself is not touched.

**Will This Play on My Device?.** First, type the device you mean, such as an iPhone, a car stereo or an Echo, or leave it empty for the usual ones; Cancel sends nothing. Then the AI's answer, from the queued files' details only: for each kind of file, yes or no and why, and what to choose in Convert to when it will not play. Copy puts the answer on the clipboard.

**Windows titled "Help:...".** This is the help window itself: the purpose of the window you were in, then the control you were on. Escape returns you to it.

### Every authored control help sentence

#### QuillConverterFrame (`quill/apps/converter.py`)

- `self._list`: The queue. Every file here is converted when you press Convert, and a folder brings the audio and video files inside it, subfolders included. Delete removes the highlighted row, Alt+Up and Alt+Down move it, and Alt+Enter describes the file. You can also paste files copied in File Explorer, or drop them here. Nothing is ever deleted from disk.
- `self._add_files_btn`: Choose audio or video files to add to the queue. You may select several at once, and adding the same file twice queues it once.
- `self._add_folder_btn`: Add a whole folder to the queue. Every audio and video file inside it is converted, subfolders included, and the folder layout is reproduced in the output folder.
- `self._remove_btn`: Take the highlighted row out of the queue. Delete does the same thing from the list itself. Nothing is removed from disk.
- `self._format`: The format every queued file becomes: sound formats first, then video. A video file converted to a sound format keeps its sound; converted to a video format it stays a video. Only the formats this computer can actually write are listed.
- `self._preset`: How the result is made. For a sound format: quality settings -- bit rate, sample rate and channels -- chosen for a purpose, so you do not have to know any of them. For a video format: how hard to work at keeping picture detail, and how large the picture may be. The format above always wins over a preset's own.
- `self._effect`: What to do to the sound on the way through, named for the problem it solves: clean up speech, make a podcast or an ACX audiobook, bring film dialogue forward, remove hum or noise, even out loud and quiet parts. Custom uses whatever you set in Custom Effects. Effects apply to the sound of video conversions too. Preview lets you hear them before you convert.
- `self._effects_btn`: Every effect on one page, starting from the recipe chosen now: noise, hum, rumble, de-essing, voice clarity, bass and treble, dialogue boost, compression, leveling, loudness target, gain, speed, fades, and keeping only part of each file.
- `self._chapters`: Where the converted files' chapter marks come from: each file's own chapters, a chapter list you wrote beside the file (book.cue, book.chapters.txt with lines like 0:00 Introduction, Audacity labels, or chapters.json), chapters found at the pauses, one every few minutes, or none. Chapters land in every format that can hold them; for the ones that cannot, such as WAV, a .cue sheet is written beside the file. Split by Chapters and Join use the same choice.
- `self._workbench_btn`: Open the highlighted MP3, M4B or M4A in the Chapter Workbench: hear it, add, rename, move and merge chapters at the playhead, find them at pauses, import or export chapter lists, and save them into the file itself.
- `self._dest`: Where the converted files are written. Leave it empty and they go into a folder named Converted beside the first file in the queue. An existing file is never overwritten: a converted file that would collide is numbered instead.
- `self._browse_btn`: Pick the output folder with a folder chooser.
- `self._convert_btn`: Convert everything in the queue with the choices above. Progress is announced every quarter, the window can go to the tray while it works, and while it runs this button is Stop.
- `self._preview_btn`: Plays fifteen seconds of the highlighted file -- or the first in the queue -- exactly as it will sound after converting, effects and all. Press again to stop. Hear Original plays the same fifteen seconds untouched, so you can compare.
- `self._original_btn`: Plays the same fifteen seconds Preview does, with nothing changed. Press again to stop.
- `self._url_btn`: Paste a web address and convert its audio: one video, a whole playlist, or a channel's newest videos. The downloader is included with Quill Converter; in Safe Mode this is declined.
- `self._progress`: How far the conversion has got, counting inside each file as well as across the queue. The status bar says the same in words, with about how long is left. Empty when nothing is converting.
#### (module level) (`quill/apps/converter_advanced.py`)

- `host._recurse`: When a folder is in the queue, convert the files in its subfolders as well, and rebuild the same folder layout in the output folder. On by default.
#### ConverterEffectsDialog (`quill/ui/converter_dialogs.py`)

- `self._loudness`: Makes every file the same perceived loudness. -16 LUFS suits podcasts and phones, -20 is Audible's ACX window, -14 is where music services play, and -23 is the television and radio standard.
#### ConverterTextDialog (`quill/ui/converter_dialogs.py`)

- `self._body`: Read-only. Arrow through it line by line, or press Copy to put all of it on the clipboard -- for an email to support, for example.
- `copy_btn`: Puts the whole report on the clipboard.
- `close_btn`: Closes this window.
#### ConverterLinkDialog (`quill/ui/converter_dialogs.py`)

- `self._count`: How many videos to take. A channel is newest first and can hold thousands, so it starts at the newest 25; a playlist keeps its order.
- `self._only_new`: Quill Converter remembers what it has downloaded from each playlist and channel, so the next time you paste the same link it fetches only what is new. Clear this to download everything again.
- `self._scope`: The link points at one video inside a playlist. Choose the video alone, or every video in the playlist.
- `self._section`: Which part of the channel: its videos, its Shorts, or its past live streams. Only the sections this channel has are listed.
- `self._since`: Only videos published in this window of time. Together with How many, whichever limit is reached first ends the download.
#### AuphonicDialog (`quill/ui/converter_auphonic_dialog.py`)

- `self._mode`: Separate productions process each file on its own with the same preset, one after another. A multitrack production mixes the files together as tracks -- several microphones of one conversation, say -- into one result.
- `self._title`: The multitrack production's title, which also names the folder its result is saved in. It starts as the first file's name. Separate productions use each file's own title instead.
- `self._token`: Your Auphonic API token, from the account settings page on auphonic.com. It is the same token the Audio Studio uses, kept in Windows Credential Manager and never in Quill Converter's settings.
- `self._remember`: When checked, sending stores the token in Windows Credential Manager, where the Audio Studio and QUILL find it too. Clear it to use the token for this time only; a token already stored stays stored.
- `self._check_btn`: Asks Auphonic who the token belongs to, how many credits are left, and which presets you have saved. Nothing is uploaded.
- `self._status`: What the last account check found: the account name and its credits, or what went wrong. Read-only.
- `self._preset`: Which of your saved Auphonic presets every production uses, or your account's default. Check Account and Load Presets fills the list; the preset you used last time is offered until then.
- `self._processing`: Keep whatever the preset does, or use Quick cleanup instead: Auphonic's filtering, leveling and loudness normalization at its usual settings.
- `self._denoise`: Quick cleanup only. Lets Auphonic take out steady background noise. It can also change quiet background sounds you wanted to keep, so it is off unless you turn it on.
- `self._format`: The format the results come back in: whatever the preset says, or one format for every production. A multitrack production saves only the final mix.
#### AuphonicConfirmDialog (`quill/ui/converter_auphonic_dialog.py`)

- `self._body`: Everything this submission does, read-only: the service, every file sent and every file left out, the preset and processing, and where the results are saved. Nothing has been uploaded yet.
#### AuphonicWaitingDialog (`quill/ui/converter_auphonic_dialog.py`)

- `self._list`: Productions Auphonic accepted whose results have not been saved yet, remembered on this computer. Nothing has contacted Auphonic to make this list.
- `resume`: Contacts Auphonic for every production listed, waits for any still processing, and saves the results where each one was going.
- `self._dismiss_btn`: Forgets the highlighted production on this computer. It stays in your Auphonic account, and nothing is deleted there.
- `close`: Closes this window; the list is kept for next time.
#### AuphonicDialog (`quill/ui/converter_auphonic_dialog.py`)

- `ok`: Shows everything that will be sent, and where the results go, before anything is uploaded.

## Quill Beacon

Control coverage: 127 audited sites (127 helped).

### Every window, and what it is for

**AI Usage.** How much each AI you have set up has been used, one sentence each, and whose count it is. Manage Usage opens the selected one's own page.

**Accessibility Settings.** How the app speaks and looks: announcement verbosity, high contrast, text scale, and reduced motion. Apply puts the settings into effect across the whole window and announces the result.

**Add Attachment.** Attach one thing to the selected bookmark: a file on disk, a URL, or an inline note. Pick the kind first; the form shows the field that kind needs. Attachments stay on this machine and are never synced.

**Add Bookmark to QuillBeacon.** Save something new: a web address or a file path, with an optional title, note, collection, and tags. Only the address is required. New bookmarks land in the Inbox unless a routing rule files them into a folder.

**Add Radio Program.** Save a radio program with its schedule: station, program name, host, start and end times in 24-hour HH:MM, and an optional stream address. A station or a program name is enough to save.

**Ask.** A conversation about what you have saved, on whichever AI is in use. When a search is typed, the search and its results' titles and notes go with every message; otherwise the selected beacon's title, note and tags do -- never where your library or any file is kept. Type in Your message and press Enter; the reply is read aloud and added to the conversation above.

**Build Search.** A form that writes the search query for you: words, an exact phrase, exclusions, type, collection, tag, link health, and domain. Search runs the built query in the main window's search box, where it can also be saved as a Smart Collection.

**Choose Your AI.** Choose where QuillBeacon's AI comes from: QUILL's free AI, your ChatGPT plan, GitHub Copilot, Codex or your own key. QuillBeacon signs in on its own, as QUILL Beacon. The list says which is in use; Enter uses the selected one or signs in to it, and Delete signs a signed-in one out.

**Collection Editor.** Create a collection, or edit the one selected in the sidebar: its name, description, optional parent, sharing mark, and color. Collections are folders you invent; a bookmark can sit in several.

**Command Palette.** Every command in the app as one searchable list. Type part of a name to filter, Enter runs the highlighted command, Escape closes without running anything.

**Describe a Saved Picture.** The AI's description of the selected beacon's picture. The words in the picture were read on this computer first and sent with it. Copy puts the description on the clipboard, and you are asked once whether to add it to the beacon's note.

**External Player.** Which media player handles handoffs: the default player, optional paths to VLC and mpv for installs not on PATH, and a per-type override so radio and podcasts can open in different players.

**Preferences.** Every setting in one place. The list on the left picks a section -- Accessibility, Sync, Capture Bridge, Published Pages, Routing Rules -- and Apply saves the inline fields; buttons inside the panels act immediately.

**Publish Collection.** Turn one collection into a read-only web page and manage it: publish, unpublish, and copy the local preview address. The preview is served by the capture bridge on this machine; publishing again refreshes the page with the collection's current contents.

**QuillBeacon.** The main window: your whole library of bookmarks -- web pages, files, podcasts, radio streams -- in three panes. The sidebar chooses where you are looking, the list shows what is there, and the details pane reads out everything saved about the selected row. Everything is local-first: nothing needs an account.

**QuillBeacon Player.** The built-in player for one episode or stream, with its chapters and transcript. Selecting a chapter jumps playback there, and Add Time Point saves a bookmark at the exact moment you are hearing so you can come back to it.

**Read on This Computer.** The words read in the selected beacon's picture on this computer, because the AI in use cannot see pictures. Nothing was sent. Copy puts the words on the clipboard.

**Review Location Repair.** A saved location resolved poorly, and this is the decision: read what was saved against what the repair engine proposes, then accept the repair, keep the old location, or mark the bookmark broken for later. Nothing is rewritten without your choice.

**Routing Rule.** One filing rule: when a new web bookmark's address contains the keyword, it is filed into the folder. The first matching rule in the Preferences list wins, and each keyword may be used only once.

**Sign In to Your AI.** Sign in to the AI you chose. Open the Page takes you to its sign-in page; approve there, and this closes itself once you are signed in.

**Smart Collection Editor.** One saved search, editable: its name, the live query it evaluates, the sort order, and an optional collection scope. The collection re-runs the query every time it is opened, so it stays current by itself.

**Smart Collections.** Your saved searches, managed: edit one's name, query, sort, or scope, or delete it. Deleting a smart collection never touches the bookmarks it matched -- it is only the saved search that goes.

**Status Center.** How the app is doing, in one readable report: the capture bridge, sync transport and vault state, library and trash counts, and how many bookmarks need attention. Refresh re-reads it; nothing here changes anything.

**Sync History.** What sync has done and what it needs from you: the commit log, the conflicts waiting for a Local/Remote/Merged decision, and the pre-sync snapshots you can roll the library back to.

**Sync Settings.** Everything sync in one dialog: the transport (off, a shared folder, or a hosted server), magic-link sign-in, and the end-to-end encryption vault. Off is the default -- nothing touches the network until you configure it here.

**Trail Editor.** Build or edit a learning trail: a titled, ordered list of bookmarks, each step with its own note. Steps are added from whatever is selected in the main window's list, and reordered with Up and Down -- no dragging anywhere.

**Windows titled "Attachments -- ...".** The files, URLs, and notes attached to this one bookmark. View opens the selected attachment, Add attaches something new, and Remove takes one off the bookmark without deleting any file on disk.

**Windows titled "Help:...".** This is the help window itself: the purpose of the window you were in, then the control you were on. Escape returns you to it.

**Windows titled "Trail -- ...".** Step through this trail one bookmark at a time. The list shows every step with its completion mark, Mark Complete toggles the current one, and Open Current opens its bookmark. Your place and progress are saved as you go.

### Every authored control help sentence

#### BeaconFrame (`quill/apps/beacon/app.py`)

- `self.dest_list`: Where you are looking: the built-in destinations (Inbox, All Bookmarks, Favorites, Trash...), then your collections, [smart] saved searches, and > trails with their progress counts. Selecting a row scopes the bookmark list to it; selecting a trail opens its step-through window instead.
- `self.new_col_btn`: Create a new, empty collection: you are asked for its name and it appears in the sidebar at once. Bookmarks are filed into it with Add to Collection (Ctrl+L) or a routing rule.
- `self.search_box`: Search the library with plain words or the query grammar: type:episode, tag:research, collection:"News", health:broken, domain:example.com, not:word, has:note. Results update as you type; Down arrow moves into them and Escape clears the search.
- `self.sort_combo`: The order of the bookmark list: added (newest first, the default), title, opened (most recently opened), mostOpened, type, health, or relevance. The list re-sorts the moment you choose.
- `self.results`: One row per bookmark with its type, location, collection, tags, date, and link health. Enter opens the row with its normal program or browser, Delete moves it to Trash, F2 renames it, and Ctrl+Space or Shift+arrows select several rows for the Bulk commands on the Edit menu.
- `self.details`: Everything stored about the selected bookmark, as read-only text you can review and copy: address, health, favorite mark, tags, collections, dates, note, saved locations, and related bookmarks. It follows the selection in the list.
#### CommandPalette (`quill/apps/beacon/commands.py`)

- `self.filter`: Type part of a command's name to filter the list below. Enter runs the highlighted command, Down arrow moves into the list, Escape closes without running anything.
- `self.list`: Every command in the app, with its keyboard shortcut in parentheses when it has one. Enter or double-click runs the selected command.
#### QuickCaptureDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.save`: Save the bookmark to your library and close. New bookmarks land in the Inbox unless a routing rule files them into a folder.
- `self.save_open`: Save the bookmark, then open it at once with your browser or the file's own program.
- `cancel`: Close without saving anything.
#### BuildSearchDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `save_smart`: Build the query and hand it to the main window's search box, ready to keep: Save Search as Smart Collection (Ctrl+Shift+G) then names and saves it as a live saved search.
- `ok`: Build the query from the filled fields and run it in the main window's search box. Empty fields are simply left out.
- `cancel`: Close without searching.
#### CollectionEditorDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `save`: Check the name and save the collection. Editing keeps the bookmarks already filed in it.
#### PublishDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.url`: The local preview address of the published page, served by the capture bridge on this machine. Read-only: Copy URL puts it on the clipboard, and it stays empty until the collection is published and the bridge is running.
- `self.publish_btn`: Write the collection out as a read-only web page and show its preview address. Publishing again refreshes the page with the collection's current contents.
- `self.unpublish_btn`: Take the published page down. The collection itself is untouched.
- `self.copy_btn`: Copy the preview address to the clipboard. Enabled only while the page is published and the capture bridge is running.
- `close_btn`: Close this window; the published state stays as shown.
#### TrailEditorDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.step_list`: The trail's steps in order: each row shows its number, a [done] mark when completed, and the bookmark it points to. Select a row, then use Up, Down, or Remove.
- `self.step_note`: The note for the next step you add: fill it in before pressing Add Selected Beacon. It is shown when stepping through the trail. Optional.
- `add_btn`: Add the bookmark currently selected in the main window's list as the trail's next step, carrying the note from the note field.
- `up_btn`: Move the selected step one position earlier in the trail.
- `down_btn`: Move the selected step one position later in the trail.
- `rm_btn`: Remove the selected step from the trail. The bookmark itself is not touched.
- `save`: Save the trail with its steps in their shown order, and close.
- `cancel`: Close without saving.
#### RepairReviewDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `info`: What the repair engine found, as read-only text: the resolution layer and its confidence, the previously saved location, and the proposed new position. Read it, then choose one of the buttons below.
- `accept`: Apply the proposed position to the saved location. Choose this when the summary matches where the content actually is now.
- `keep`: Leave the saved location exactly as it was.
- `broken`: Keep the old location but mark the bookmark broken, so it shows under Needs Attention until you deal with it.
- `cancel`: Close without changing anything.
#### RadioProgramDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `save`: Save the program to your library and close.
- `cancel`: Close without saving.
#### StatusCenterDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.text`: The current report, one line per fact: capture bridge, sync transport and vault state, library and trash counts, and how many bookmarks need attention. Read-only; Refresh re-reads it.
- `refresh`: Re-read every status line right now; the result is announced.
- `close`: Close the Status Center. Nothing here changes anything.
#### PreferencesDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.sections`: The preference sections. Selecting one shows its panel to the right: Accessibility, Sync, Capture Bridge, Published Pages, or Routing Rules.
- `apply_btn`: Apply the inline settings -- the accessibility fields and the auto-sync interval -- and close. Buttons inside the panels (sync, copy token, unpublish, routing edits) have already acted when pressed.
- `cancel_btn`: Close without applying the inline settings. Panel actions already taken are not rolled back.
- `self.verbosity`: How much QuillBeacon announces on its own: minimal keeps to the essentials, normal (the default) adds confirmations, verbose adds position and detail lines. Takes effect on Apply.
- `self.scale`: The text size for the whole window, as a percentage of normal. Takes effect on Apply.
- `self.auto_sync`: How often to sync automatically. Off, the default, never touches the network by itself; a timed interval runs only once sync is configured and the vault is unlocked. Takes effect on Apply.
- `sync_settings_btn`: Open the full Sync Settings dialog now: transport, sign-in, and the encryption vault.
- `sync_now_btn`: Push and pull changes right now, using the saved sync settings.
- `self.bridge_url`: The local address the capture bridge is listening on, for a browser extension's options page. Read-only; it shows (not running) when the bridge is off.
- `self.bridge_token`: The secret a browser extension must present to the bridge. Read-only; Copy Token takes it to the clipboard.
- `copy_btn`: Copy the bridge token to the clipboard, ready to paste into the extension's options.
- `self._pub_list`: Every collection currently published as a read-only page, with its item count. Select one to unpublish it.
- `unpublish_btn`: Take the selected page down immediately. The collection itself is untouched.
- `self._routing_list`: The filing rules, in the order they are tried -- the first matching keyword wins. Each row reads keyword files into folder. Select a rule to edit, remove, or reorder it.
#### RoutingRuleDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.keyword`: The text to look for in a new web bookmark's address -- a domain like example.com, or any fragment. Matching is a simple contains, and each keyword may be used by only one rule. Required.
- `self.collection`: The folder matching bookmarks are filed into. Pick an existing collection or type a new name. Required.
- `ok`: Save the rule. Both the keyword and the folder are required.
- `cancel`: Close without saving.
#### A11ySettingsDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.verbosity`: How much QuillBeacon announces on its own: minimal keeps to the essentials, normal (the default) adds confirmations, verbose adds position and detail lines. Takes effect on Apply.
- `self.scale`: The text size for the whole window, as a percentage of normal. Takes effect on Apply.
- `save`: Apply the settings to the whole app and save them; the result is announced.
- `cancel`: Close without changing anything.
#### SmartCollectionsDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.list`: Your saved searches, one per row with the query each one runs. Double-click or Edit opens the editor for the selected row.
- `self.edit_btn`: Open the selected smart collection in the editor to change its name, query, sort, or scope.
- `self.delete_btn`: Delete the selected smart collection after a confirmation. The bookmarks it matched are not affected.
- `close`: Close this manager; the sidebar refreshes on return.
#### SmartCollectionEditorDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.name`: The smart collection's name, shown in the sidebar with a [smart] mark. Required.
- `self.query`: The live search this collection evaluates each time it is opened, in the search box's grammar -- for example tag:research not:archived. Required.
- `self.sort`: The order results are listed in when this collection is opened. added, the default, puts the newest first.
- `self.scope`: Limit the search to one collection, by name. Blank searches the whole library.
- `ok`: Save the changes to this saved search. Name and query are both required.
- `cancel`: Close without saving.
#### TrailStepDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.list`: The trail's steps in order. The * marks your current step and [x] a completed one; selecting a row makes it current, and double-clicking opens its bookmark.
- `self.note`: The note saved with the current step, read-only here. Notes are written in the Trail Editor.
- `self.prev_btn`: Move to the previous step. Your place in the trail is saved as you move.
- `self.next_btn`: Move to the next step. Your place in the trail is saved as you move.
- `self.complete_btn`: Toggle whether the current step is completed. Progress is saved immediately and shown in the sidebar's count.
- `self.open_btn`: Open the current step's bookmark with its normal program or browser, keeping this trail window open.
- `close`: Close the trail. Your place and completion marks are already saved.
#### AttachmentsDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.list`: The files, URLs, and notes attached to this bookmark, one per row with its kind in brackets. Double-click or View opens the selected one.
- `self.add_btn`: Attach something new to this bookmark: a file on disk, a URL, or an inline note.
- `self.view_btn`: Open the selected attachment: a note is shown in place, a file or URL opens with its normal program.
- `self.remove_btn`: Remove the selected attachment after a confirmation. A file attachment's file on disk is not deleted.
- `close`: Close the attachments window.
#### AttachmentAddDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.name`: A display name for the attachment. Left blank, the list shows the file name, the URL, or the note's first words. Optional.
- `self.path`: The full path of the file to attach. The file stays where it is -- only its path is stored, and attachments never sync.
- `self.browse`: Pick the file with the standard file chooser instead of typing its path.
- `self.url`: The web address to attach to the bookmark.
- `self.note`: The note's text, stored inside the library with the bookmark.
- `ok`: Attach it. The field that must be filled is the one for the kind chosen above: path, URL, or note text.
- `cancel`: Close without attaching anything.
#### SyncSettingsDialog (`quill/apps/beacon/dialogs.py`)

- `self.folder`: The folder your devices sync through -- typically one inside iCloud Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox. Used only when the transport is Folder.
- `self.browse`: Pick the sync folder with the standard chooser instead of typing its path.
- `self.send_link`: Save the settings above and ask the server to email a sign-in link to that address. No password exists to remember.
